title: Daily routine
goal: Describe your day and habits, say how often you do things, and say what you're doing right now.
intro:
This is the unit where Marathi verbs really come alive. The **present habitual** (मी उठतो 'I get up') describes routines and general truths; the **present continuous** (मी जेवतोय 'I'm eating') describes what's happening now.

Both change for the speaker's gender: a man says मी जातो, a woman says मी जाते. Listen for this from now on — it's one of the first things Marathi speakers notice in a learner.

grammar.title: Present habitual: मी करतो / करते
grammar.body:
Stem (infinitive minus **-णे**) + **त** + personal ending. The ending shows person, number and — in the singular — gender:

मी कर**तो** (m) / कर**ते** (f) — I do
तू कर**तोस** (m) / कर**तेस** (f) — you do
तो कर**तो** · ती कर**ते** · ते (n) कर**तं** — he / she / it does
आम्ही कर**तो** — we do
तुम्ही कर**ता** — you (pol./pl.) do
ते / त्या कर**तात** — they do

**Negative:** stem + **त नाही** (+ person ending on नाही): मी करत नाही, तू करत नाहीस, ते करत नाहीत.

Use it for habits, routines and general facts: मी चहा पितो 'I drink tea (habitually)'. Stems ending in a vowel just add त: जा → जातो, खा → खातो, ये → येतो, धु → धुतो.

examples.en: Do you read Marathi? (to a man)

grammar.title: Present continuous: करत आहे → करतोय
grammar.body:
For an action happening right now, use stem + **त** + the present of असणे: मी करत **आहे**, तू करत **आहेस**, ते करत **आहेत**.

In speech this fuses into a short form, and **gender comes back**:
मी करतोय (m) / करतेय (f)
तू करतोयस (m) / करतेयस (f)
तो करतोय · ती करतेय · ते (n) करतंय
आम्ही करतोय · तुम्ही करताय · ते करतायत

The formal written form करत आहे is fine everywhere; the fused form is what you will hear. Note: Marathi often uses the continuous for feelings and states too: मला भूक लागतेय, डोकं दुखतंय.

examples.en: I'm eating, I'll call you later. (man)

dialogue.title: Early bird
dialogue.setting: Two colleagues, Sunil and Rajesh, chat during a tea break.

lines.speaker: Sunil
lines.en: What time do you get up every day?

lines.speaker: Rajesh
lines.native: साधारण साडेपाच वाजता. मी आधी व्यायाम करतो.
lines.roman: sādhāraṇ sāḍepāts vādztā. mī ādhī vyāyām karto.
lines.en: About half past five. I exercise first.

lines.speaker: Sunil
lines.native: बापरे! मी तर आठ वाजता उठतो.
lines.roman: bāpre! mī tar āṭh vādztā uṭhto.
lines.en: Wow! I get up at eight.

lines.speaker: Rajesh
lines.en: So when do you get to the office?

lines.speaker: Sunil
lines.en: At ten. I come by bus.

lines.speaker: Rajesh
lines.en: And what do you do in the evening?

lines.speaker: Sunil
lines.native: घरी जातो, जेवतो आणि टीव्ही बघतो.
lines.roman: gharī dzāto, jevto āṇi ṭīvhī baghto.
lines.en: I go home, eat and watch TV.

lines.speaker: Rajesh
lines.en: And what are you doing right now?

lines.speaker: Rajesh
lines.en: Then come on, let's go for a little walk!

culture: A typical Mumbai day revolves around the local train timetable — the 'ट्रेन पकडणे' (catching the train) is a daily battle, and many office-goers carry a steel lunchbox (डबा), often delivered by Mumbai's famous डबेवाले. In Pune, an afternoon rest (वामकुक्षी) after lunch is a much-joked-about tradition; some old Pune shops still close between 1 and 4 p.m.

lessons.title: My morning

tip.title: Habits: मी उठतो / उठते
tip.body:
- For habits: stem + **त** + ending: मी उठ**तो** (m) / उठ**ते** (f), तू उठतोस, तो उठतो, ती उठते, आम्ही उठतो, तुम्ही उठ**ता**, ते उठ**तात**.
- Negative: stem + **त नाही**: मी लवकर उठत नाही.
- **आधी** 'first' and **मग** 'then' put the steps in order.

new: मी रोज सकाळी सहा वाजता उठतो.

sentences.en: I get up at seven every day. (woman)
What time do you get up?
Dad gets up early every day.

sentences.native: मी आधी दात घासतो, मग चहा पितो.
sentences.roman: mī ādhī dāt ghāsto, mag tsahā pito.
sentences.en: First I brush my teeth, then I have tea. (man)
Do the children brush their teeth every day?
She has a bath in the morning.

sentences.native: आम्ही आधी अंघोळ करतो, मग नाश्ता.
sentences.roman: āmhī ādhī aṅghoḷ karto, mag nāshtā.
sentences.en: We have a bath first, then breakfast.
On Sundays I get up late. (man)

tip.title: Leaving, arriving, coming back
tip.body:
- **निघणे** = set off. **मी निघतो / निघते** is how you say 'I'm off'.
- 'From home' = **घरातून**; 'to the office' = ऑफिस**ला**, 'to work' = काम**ाला**.
- **पोहोचणे** 'reach' and **परत येणे** 'come back' work like any verb: पोहोचतो, परत येतात.

sentences.en: What time do you leave home? (to a man)
Right, I'm off. (woman)
I get to the office at nine. (woman)
I go to work by bus. (man)

sentences.native: तुम्ही किती वाजता घरी परत येता?
sentences.roman: tumhī kitī vādztā gharī parat yetā?
sentences.en: What time do you get back home?
They come back in the evening.
There's a lot of work today.
I'll be back in five minutes. (man)

tip.title: How often?
tip.body:
- **नेहमी** always · **साधारणपणे** usually · **कधी कधी** sometimes.
- **कधीच** + negative = never: मी कधीच व्यायाम कर**त नाही**.
- **फिरायला जाणे** = go for a walk or an outing.

sentences.native: मी नेहमी आठ वाजता नाश्ता करतो.
sentences.roman: mī nehmī āṭh vādztā nāshtā karto.
sentences.en: I always have breakfast at eight. (man)
She is never late.
Do you exercise? (to a man)

sentences.native: नाही, मी कधीच व्यायाम करत नाही.
sentences.roman: nāhī, mī kadhīts vyāyām karat nāhī.
sentences.en: No, I never exercise.
We sometimes go out for a walk.
Grandpa goes for a walk every morning.

sentences.native: साधारणपणे आम्ही रात्री नऊ वाजता जेवतो.
sentences.roman: sādhāraṇpaṇe āmhī rātrī naū vādztā jevto.
sentences.en: We usually have dinner at nine.
He's always late!

tip.title: Right now: मी करतोय / करतेय
tip.body:
- For 'right now' Marathi uses **-तोय / -तेय**: मी करतोय (m) / करतेय (f), तू करतोयस, ती करतेय, तुम्ही **करताय**, ते **करतायत**.
- The formal, written form is मी करत आहे.
- Habit vs now: मी स्वयंपाक कर**तो** 'I cook' · मी स्वयंपाक कर**तोय** 'I'm cooking'.

sentences.en: What's Mum doing?
Dad is cooking.
What are you doing? (polite)
I'm working, let's talk later. (woman)
We're having dinner.
Are you eating right now? (to a man)
I cook every day. (man)
Who's cooking today?

tip.title: I'm learning Marathi
tip.body:
- **शिकणे** learn: मी मराठी **शिकतोय / शिकतेय** 'I'm learning Marathi (these days)'.
- **वाचणे** read · **लिहिणे** write · **बघणे** watch: मी रात्री टीव्ही बघतो.
- The same endings as करणे: बघतो, बघताय, बघतायत.

sentences.en: I'm learning Marathi. (woman)
What are you reading? (to a man)
I read a little Marathi every day. (man)

sentences.native: ती मराठी लिहिते, पण बोलत नाही.
sentences.roman: tī marāṭhī lihite, paṇ bolat nāhī.
sentences.en: She writes Marathi, but doesn't speak it.
The children are watching TV.
What do you watch in the evenings?
My daughter learns English at school.
I'm writing just now, give me five minutes. (man)

tip.title: Clothes and sleep
tip.body:
- **कपडे** 'clothes' is plural: कपडे **धुणे** 'do the laundry', कपडे **घालणे** 'get dressed'.
- **झोपणे** 'go to bed, sleep': तुम्ही किती वाजता झोपता?
- 'I'm sleepy' = **मला झोप येतेय** (sleep is coming to me; झोप is feminine).

sentences.en: I go to bed at eleven. (man)
The children go to bed at nine.
I'm sleepy.
When do you do your laundry? (to a man)
Mum is doing the laundry.
Get dressed quickly, we're leaving!
Are these clothes clean?
The baby's asleep, speak quietly.
